justification: Finding [0] only raises concerns about diff completeness: whether `env.canReferenceType` exists and whether the `diagnose` signature change is shown. It does not identify that the caller passes all in-scope pipes (`pipes`) rather than only the pipes used by the template, nor the resulting spurious forced-inlining. Acting on it would not lead to the fix of filtering by `boundTarget.getUsedPipes()`.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the known defect: the guard uses the generic `_placeholderRe` which SafeSelector also uses for attribute selectors and `:not(...)` content, so separators after parts like `a[href]` or `[type=text]` are wrongly skipped when the next char is a hex digit. It explicitly recommends that 'The check should only match placeholders created for backslash escapes', which is precisely what the fix does by introducing `__esc-ph-N__`. Same faulty code, same mechanism, same remedy.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the defect: the skip check matches any `__ph-N__` placeholder, including those SafeSelector uses for attribute selectors and :nth-* expressions, so a following hex character causes the combinator split to be skipped and selectors to be scoped incorrectly ("`[type=text] div` loses the scoping on `div`"). Its suggested remedy — "confirm that the placeholder is an escape ... not merely a placeholder that appears in the part" — is equivalent to the fix's introduction of a distinct `__esc-ph-N__` placeholder and checking only for it.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the known bug: the removed `if (_global.beforeEach)` / `if (_global.afterEach)` guards in test_hooks.ts, causing `ReferenceError: beforeEach is not defined` when the module loads outside a test runner (e.g. in an app/server bundle). Its suggested fix (a `typeof beforeEach === 'function'` guard) is equivalent to the actual fix using `globalThis.beforeEach?.(...)`.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the known bug: "The previous `if (_global.beforeEach)` and `if (_global.afterEach)` guards were removed, so `beforeEach(...)` and `afterEach(...)` are now called unconditionally at module load... the import throws a `ReferenceError`." This is the same faulty code in test_hooks.ts and the same failure mechanism (module evaluated outside a test runner throws). Acting on it would lead a maintainer to restore the guards, which is what the fix does via `globalThis.beforeEach?.(...)`.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the known bug: in `collectDeferredSymbols`, "`deferBlockDep.isDefaultImport` is never set. It stays at its initial `false`", and explains that the defer deps functions read that flag and thus emit `m => m.CmpA` instead of `m => m.default`, yielding undefined at runtime. Acting on it would lead directly to the fix of setting `deferBlockDep.isDefaultImport = isDefaultImport(importDecl)`.

The known bug is that `deferBlockDep.isDefaultImport` is never assigned in `collectDeferredSymbols`, so the per-block dependency keeps its initial `false` and the template-level loader emits `m.Name` instead of `m.default` for any default import. Finding [0] instead criticizes the shape-check in `isDefaultImport()` for mixed imports like `import Foo, {Bar} from './x'` ("A mixed import ... has namedBindings, so it is treated as not default"). That is a different (also plausible) defect in the helper function; acting on it would change `isDefaultImport`'s logic but would leave `deferBlockDep.isDefaultImport` unset, so the actual bug would remain. No match.

Finding [0] points at the inverted constructor branch, but its stated defect is a tabindex/accessibility regression for non-anchor hosts ("non-anchor hosts such as `<div routerLink>` never get the default `tabindex=\"0\"`"); it does not identify that the subscription gating itself is wrong, and fixing it would leave the conditional in `subscribeToNavigationEventsIfNecessary` intact, so relative links with e.g. `queryParamsHandling="replace"` would still go stale. Finding [1] says the default-handling clause is "negated" ("Conversely, it subscribes when nothing depends on router state. The logic is negated"), which is precisely the excluded case in the known bug: its fix would flip the clause and subscribe in fewer cases, the opposite of the real fix, which removes the condition entirely because relative hrefs always depend on the ActivatedRoute. Neither finding identifies that the optimization's premise is wrong and that anchor links must always subscribe.

Finding [0] identifies a different defect: the inverted constructor branch causing non-anchor hosts to lose the default tabindex ('Non-anchor hosts such as `<div routerLink>` no longer get a default tabindex'). Its suggested fix (flip the condition) would still leave the conditional subscription logic in `subscribeToNavigationEventsIfNecessary`, so relative links with e.g. `queryParamsHandling="replace"` would still go stale after navigation. Finding [1] is precisely the excluded case described in the known bug: it says 'The negation on the default should be removed', i.e. it argues the default-handling clause is inverted and would make the directive subscribe in fewer cases, the opposite of the real fix which removes the condition entirely and always subscribes for anchor elements. Neither finding recognizes that any relative link's href depends on the ActivatedRoute and thus the optimization premise itself is wrong.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the known defect: replacing `.toPromise()` with a `first()`-based `firstValueFrom` changes empty-completion behavior from resolving `undefined` to rejecting with `EmptyError`, so "a `canLoad` guard, or `loadChildren` observable that completes empty used to resolve to `undefined` and now makes navigation fail with `EmptyError`." This is the same faulty code and the same failure mechanism (empty observables now throw EmptyError and navigation fails instead of treating it as no match). Acting on this would lead a maintainer to handle EmptyError in the recognizer, equivalent to the fix. Low confidence rating does not change that the content matches.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the known bug: "cancelLeavingNodes cancels any leaving element for the same tNode whose parent differs... every instance of a component or template shares it. If instance A's element is playing its leave animation and instance B is inserted into a different parent... A's animation is cut short... removed from the DOM immediately." This is the same faulty code (the different-parent branch), the same root cause (TNode shared across instances), and the same failure (leave animation skipped on a distinct sibling instance). Acting on it would lead to distinguishing logical views, which is what the fix does via declaration view tracking. Finding [1] concerns leavingNodes entries lingering/memory growth on Detach — a different issue. Finding [2] concerns the dropped removeAnimationsFromQueue call for enter animations — a different concern unrelated to the cross-parent force-removal bug.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the known bug: 'A TNode is shared by every instance of a template or component, but `cancelLeavingNodes` cancels any leaving element whose parent differs from the new element's parent... Instance 1's leave animation is forcibly cancelled and its element removed early, although the two are unrelated.' This is the same faulty code (the cross-parent branch in `cancelLeavingNodes`) and the same mechanism (TNode shared across distinct instances), and acting on it would lead a maintainer to distinguish instances by their owning/declaration view, as the fix does. Finding [1] concerns a different issue (stale entries in `leavingNodes` leaking when `clearLeavingNodes` isn't called), not the cross-parent cancellation of distinct instances. Finding [2] concerns the removal of `removeAnimationsFromQueue` and pending enter animations, which is an unrelated concern.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the known bug: "`position` is an `ElementPosition` (number[]). The old template literal turned it into a comma-separated string such as '0,1,2'. `stringifyAndEscape` now yields the string literal "[0,1,2]"... The receiving `findConstructorByPosition` does not appear to be updated... most likely still parses with `split(',').map(parseInt)`" — this is precisely the wire-format mismatch fixed by updating `findNodeFromSerializedPosition` to use `JSON.parse`. Finding [1] identifies the same mechanism for `findDomElementByPosition` ("now receives the string "[0,1,2]" instead of '0,1,2'... selecting a DOM element from the component tree breaks"), which is the other half of the same bug. Acting on either finding would lead a maintainer to update the backend parser, matching the fix.

Finding [0] identifies exactly the known bug: `stringifyAndEscape(position)` changes the wire format from comma-separated "0,1,2" to JSON "[0,1,2]", and "If `findConstructorByPosition` still parses its input with `split(',')` and `parseInt`... The element lookup then fails and view-source stops working. The receiving side is not updated in this diff. The same applies to `findDomElementByPosition`." This points directly to the backend parser (`findNodeFromSerializedPosition`) needing to be updated to JSON.parse, which is what the fix does.
